- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above prior peak.
- If history shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops), model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid mean reversion underestimation.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.5), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for potential rebound.
- Model consistently underestimates in early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days of 30d forecast) — apply a 1–2% upward bias for first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows 2+ consecutive 0.00 values, model tends to be overly conservative; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid lagged underreaction.
